MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
DEVOPS & PLATFORM ENGINEERING | QA AUTOMATION
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including recent hands-on work in CI/CD, Kubernetes-based test environments, infrastructure tooling and observability. Owns GitLab CI pipelines serving three product teams and has delivered ephemeral environments, measurable pipeline improvements and test metrics dashboards. Builds personal Kubernetes and GitOps infrastructure, including Terraform-provisioned Hetzner VPS infrastructure. Currently studying for the Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) exam.

CORE SKILLS
Infrastructure & delivery: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes, k3s, Argo CD, Terraform (personal project), Ansible (basic)
Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki; dashboards for test and pipeline metrics
Programming & data: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL, PostgreSQL
Platforms & tooling: Linux, Git, AWS (EC2 and S3 basics; personal learning)
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software | Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (~25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, as well as artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end testing into its own stage; monthly CI runner costs fell by about 30%.
- Built merge-request ephemeral environments with Docker Compose and later Helm on the shared Kubernetes cluster, including application services, PostgreSQL and seeded data. Environments are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Developed Bash and Python tooling for PostgreSQL test-data seeding and collected CI test results for Grafana dashboards showing flaky tests by team.
- Wrote an internal guide to how CI works, now used in team onboarding; mentored two QA interns in 2023.
- Work with namespace-level access on the shared Kubernetes cluster; develop Helm charts for test environments.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House | Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications for client projects through manual and automated testing.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, reproducing bugs for developers.

SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS

Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Built a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 cluster running k3s, with applications deployed from a Git repository using Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform in a personal account; used Ansible at a basic level.

Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health | 2023–2024
- Delivered short-lived environments for each merge request, deployed via GitLab CI and Helm to the shared Kubernetes cluster.
- Enabled QA and product teams to review features before merge, with end-to-end tests running against the environment; automated cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Technologies: GitLab CI, Helm, Kubernetes, Docker, Bash, PostgreSQL.

CI Pipeline Speed-up | Odrava Health | 2022
- Profiled pipelines across three teams, parallelised test jobs, added dependency caching and split end-to-end tests into a separate stage.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.
- Technologies: GitLab CI, Docker, pytest-xdist.

Flaky Test Dashboard | Odrava Health | 2023
- Collected CI test results in PostgreSQL and built Grafana dashboards to show flaky tests by team, supporting investigation and prioritisation of recurring failures.
- Flaky-test rate fell from 7% to below 1% after teams addressed the most frequent offenders.
- Technologies: Python, PostgreSQL, Grafana, GitLab API.

EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATIONS & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | Studying; exam scheduled for January 2027

LANGUAGES
Polish (native) | English (C1) | German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from QA automation into DevOps and platform engineering. The strongest evidence is quantified and credible: pipeline duration reduced from 38 to 14 minutes, runner costs reduced by about 30%, flaky tests reduced from 7% to below 1%, and ownership of CI pipelines for three product teams. The selected infrastructure projects add useful depth and demonstrate initiative, observability, GitOps, Kubernetes and Terraform exposure. The main content limitation is that the CV presents a developing infrastructure profile rather than a fully experienced cloud infrastructure engineer: the scope of Kubernetes access, Terraform use and AWS exposure is correctly disclosed but does not meet several senior requirements in the advertisement.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: ATS compatibility is very good. The CV uses conventional headings, chronological employment history, standard text formatting, clear keyword groupings and no apparent tables, graphics or parsing barriers. Relevant terms include GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS, Linux, PostgreSQL, observability, Prometheus, Grafana and Argo CD. AI screening probability is moderate to good for junior or mid-level DevOps/platform roles, but likely lower for this specific contractor role because the advertisement places heavy emphasis on strong Terraform and Terragrunt, AWS or equivalent cloud operation, systems design, networking, mTLS and security. Terragrunt and mTLS are absent appropriately because the candidate's information does not support them.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the role's engineering-led and ownership-oriented aspects. Owning pipelines for three teams, building ephemeral environments, writing onboarding documentation, mentoring interns and creating measurable improvements support leadership, analytical thinking, collaboration and clear communication. Kubernetes, Helm, GitLab CI, Linux, monitoring and a Terraform-provisioned Hetzner VPS provide relevant adjacent experience. However, the candidate's material shows gaps against the role's core infrastructure expectations: no Terragrunt, no demonstrated strong Terraform practice, no mTLS experience, limited AWS exposure, no demonstrated production cloud operation or cluster administration, and no IoT, automotive or remote-device integration. The material also does not establish backend or full-stack experience beyond Java test code. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than defects that can be solved by rewriting the CV.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary section, make the target positioning more directly relevant to the role without overstating seniority. Replace the opening with wording such as: "QA automation engineer transitioning into DevOps and platform engineering, with 7 years of experience and recent hands-on work in CI/CD, Kubernetes-based environments, infrastructure tooling and observability." Keep the existing quantified pipeline and ephemeral-environment achievements after it.
2. In the Core Skills section under "Infrastructure & delivery," change "Terraform (personal project)" to "Terraform (personal Hetzner VPS infrastructure)". This preserves the truthful scope while making the supported infrastructure-as-code experience more searchable and specific.
3. In the Core Skills section, change "AWS (EC2 and S3 basics; personal learning)" to "AWS: EC2 and S3 basics through personal learning". This makes the level and context immediately clear to a recruiter and avoids any impression of professional AWS production experience.
4. In the Selected Infrastructure Projects section under "Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps," clarify the networking and security-related evidence by changing the second bullet to: "Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS certificate management." Do not add mTLS or broader network-security claims, because those are not supported by the candidate information.
5. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, make the stakeholder and communication evidence more explicit by revising the onboarding bullet to: "Wrote an internal guide explaining how CI works, now used for team onboarding; mentored two QA interns in 2023." This uses the candidate's existing evidence and better supports the requirement concerning clear communication and bringing others along.
6. In the Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments project, retain the sentence that QA and product teams could review features before merge. It is valuable evidence of collaboration and stakeholder enablement. Consider moving this project immediately after the current Odrava role if the CV is being tailored specifically for this vacancy, so the most relevant infrastructure work is encountered earlier.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from QA automation into DevOps and platform engineering. The strongest evidence is specific and quantified: pipeline time reduced from 38 to 14 minutes, runner costs reduced by approximately 30%, flaky tests reduced from 7% to below 1%, and ownership of CI pipelines serving three product teams. The infrastructure projects make the career transition credible and demonstrate practical Kubernetes, GitOps, observability and Terraform exposure. The main limitation is that the document presents a strong junior-to-mid DevOps transition profile rather than a close match for a cloud infrastructure contractor expected to design and operate production cloud systems independently.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses conventional section headings, readable text, standard employment formatting, explicit technology names and measurable achievements. The headline and summary contain relevant terms such as DevOps, platform engineering, CI/CD, Kubernetes, infrastructure tooling and observability. Likely AI/ATS screening probability is moderate to high for junior or transition-level DevOps/platform roles, but moderate for this particular vacancy because the document does not demonstrate Terragrunt, mTLS, system design, production cloud operation or strong AWS experience. The use of 'Terraform (personal project)' and 'AWS ... personal learning' is appropriately transparent and should be retained. There are no apparent formatting or parsing defects.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with hands-on CI/CD infrastructure, Kubernetes-based environments, observability, Linux, analytical problem solving, technical ownership and communication. It also shows experience bringing stakeholders along through environments used by QA and product teams, onboarding documentation and mentoring. However, the candidate's own material confirms substantial gaps against the role's core requirements: no Terragrunt, no mTLS experience, limited cloud exposure, no production cluster ownership, no production on-call experience and no IoT, automotive or remote-device integration. Terraform is practical but personal and not strong commercial Terraform experience. The candidate has relevant JVM exposure through Java test automation, but not backend or full-stack JVM development. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than defects that can be solved by rewriting the CV.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the level and scope of cloud exposure even more precise while strengthening the target positioning. For example, change the opening to: "QA automation engineer transitioning into DevOps and platform engineering, with 7 years of software engineering experience and recent hands-on ownership of GitLab CI, Kubernetes-based test environments, infrastructure tooling and observability." Retain the existing evidence about three product teams and quantified pipeline improvements.
2. In the Core Skills section, change "Terraform (personal project)" to "Terraform (personal Hetzner infrastructure project)" and change "AWS (EC2 and S3 basics; personal learning)" to "AWS: EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning)". This preserves ATS keywords while preventing recruiters from interpreting these as substantial commercial cloud experience.
3. In the Odrava Health experience section, add the scope limitation directly to the Kubernetes bullets: "Work with namespace-level access on the shared Kubernetes cluster; develop Helm charts and deploy test environments rather than administering the cluster itself." This is already supported by the candidate information and avoids implying cluster ownership.
4. In the Selected Infrastructure Projects section, add an architecture-oriented sentence to the Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments project, using only the documented facts: "Designed the environment composition around the application services, PostgreSQL, seeded data and automated lifecycle cleanup, with GitLab CI coordinating Helm deployment and end-to-end test execution." This makes the existing system-design evidence easier for the recruiter and ATS to identify without claiming broader architecture experience.
5. In the CKA entry, retain the qualification as future study only and use the clearest wording: "Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) — exam scheduled for January 2027; not yet certified." This is more explicit for automated and human screening.
